name: TM-Env
description: Oracle-verified Terra Mystica self-play environment for long-horizon multi-agent reinforcement learning. Used a PettingZoo AEC wrapper and a Gymnasium single-agent wrapper with legal action masks, seeded determinism, serializable states, and optimized reward formulation on 29M logged transitions for offline RL. Built baseline score from random play through a max^n MCTS self-play agent over a shared policy/value network; 10^6+ parallelized self-play simulations of max^n search with human-regularized RL produced an agent that consistently beats scores from the top 1% of human players.

name: bgelo
description: Glicko-1 rating engine for multiplayer board games, decomposing n-player results into 1v1 matchups weighted by game complexity, relative familiarity, elo spread, and duration. Algorithm auto-tuned by backtester that scores pre-play forecasts to tune weighting mechanisms. Currently forecaster accurately calls 62.5% of decisive pairwise matchups against a 50% baseline. Accuracy should improve with data, currently very low sample-size (n<10 for most games).

name: ercot-nodal
description: Eight-bus security-constrained dispatch model of ERCOT, built to work out how locational prices actually form and where grid-scale or residential storage is worth siting. Each hour is a linear program over a DC network with two generic transmission constraints and reserves co-optimised against a demand curve; every bus price is read off the duals as the system lambda minus its shift-factor-weighted shadow prices. A home-battery fleet is layered on as a price taker, its schedule and the resulting price iterated to a fixed point by the method of successive averages. Verified rather than trusted: shift factors reproduce an independently coded DC power flow, and the price at every bus equals the finite-difference derivative of total dispatch cost with respect to load there. Finds that congestion lives in surplus hours rather than peak ones, and that the cheapest bus on the system is the worst place to put a battery — a binding export constraint moves the price level, not the time spread storage is paid for.

name: dr.active
description: Developed a regression model using RDKit and scikit-learn's random forest to predict binding affinity (MAE) from SMILES string and target name with 70% accuracy. Subsequently implemented a Graph Neural Network to increase accuracy by 15%.

name: Ripple
description: Minnehack 2025 Finalist. Built for the theme “finding community,” users complete community-driven challenges with peer-based verification to climb local leaderboards.

name: GopherGuessr
description: Developed the frontend for a UMN-based location guessing app using JSX, React, and Tailwind to implement leaderboards, user profiles, and gameplay loop UI. Peaked at over 2,000 weekly active users and 15,000+ total guesses.

name: BioScrolls
description: Fine-tuned BioBERT and relation extraction techniques to mine multilingual biomedical literature for neurological gene-disease-drug associations, building a time-indexed knowledge graph with key metrics such as entity frequency, relationship confidence, and trend analysis over time.

name: dr.optimus
description: Developed a drug optimization pipeline using Deep Q-Networks (DQN), where the agent modifies molecular structures represented as graphs using a Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based environment; evaluated optimization success using QED (Quantitative Estimate of Drug-likeness), binding affinity scores from docking simulations (e.g., AutoDock), and toxicity predictions generated by pre-trained classification models.

name: folduzz
description: Developed a deep convolutional generative adversarial neural network to predict protein folding.
